- When sentiment is consistently negative (especially > 3 consecutive negative values), model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–10% below historical mean.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward; apply a 3–5 day lag correction to avoid premature reversal.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model frequently underestimates downward momentum; adjust forecast downward by 2–4% for the next 3–5 days.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in early forecast windows; for 30-day horizon, apply a 1–2% downward bias if recent 7-day average is above 70.
- If sentiment shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.5 for 3+ days), model tends to overestimate upside; cap forecast at 10% above recent 14-day high.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model exhibits high variance; use 3-day moving average of true values to smooth forecast deviations.
